newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German March Ifo business index.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German March Ifo business index.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after the German Ifo economics institute said its March business climate index for west Germany fell to 92.4 from 93.6 in February.

"We had forecast a decline but this drop is bigger than we had expected. But it is not that surprising given that the dollar weakened slightly in March and because of uncertainty about the outcome of discussions about corporate tax reform. But in the coming months the index should rise as the strengthened dollar should brighten export prospects. This decline is only temporary."
WOLFRAM RODDEWIG, EUROPEAN ECONOMIST AT SCHRODERS, LONDON:

"The figures are very disappointing for west Germany, where they are down quite sharply. It does seem to be a case of one sector of the economy, manufacturing, doing well but other sectors such as retailing and particularly construction still severely depressed. There is still a lack of the momemtum needed to generate growth and create employment.
"We can however be reasonably optimistic that the economy will grow at around two percent this year, but the domestic part of the economy is continuing to lag behind."
"This will no doubt raise expectations for a rate cut from the Bundesbank but I don't think that will be the case."
HANS-JUERGEN MELTZER, ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE BANK RESEARCH:

"I think this is a transitional phenomenon -- we will just have to live with a split economy (referring to disparate growth rates in different sectors of the economy). But I expect the upward trend will continue in the course of the year. Two percent growth in the economy is still likely this year and a rebound can be expected in the second quarter. First quarter GDP growth is likely to be 0.2 to 0.3 percent at most.
LUTZ WIEGAND, ECONOMIST AT BAYERSICHE VEREINSBANK:
"I also see a pick-up in the second quarter. In the first quarter we shall see about 0.2 to 0.3 percent growth in GDP."
